disposition_reason: Mouse pharmacology of an oral bismuth porphyrin: plasma Cmax 16.8 µg/L at 50 mg/kg, kidney accumulation, no or negligible BUN rise when given alone; cites plasma safety level 50 µg/L and alarm level 100 µg/L.

study.design: in vitro screening and mouse pharmacology and toxicology
study.method: Plasma and renal bismuth measured over 48 h after oral dosing (method in supplemental file, not reviewed)

material.label_as_printed: Mouse plasma bismuth after oral Bi(TPP) 50 mg/kg

findings.group: Mice, single oral dose of bismuth tetraphenylporphyrinate 50 mg/kg; 3 mice per time point
findings.reported: Cmax 16.8 µg/L at Tmax 1 h; AUC0-48h 370.2 h·µg/L; t1/2 about 6 h
findings.notes: Animal pharmacokinetic value for a synthetic drug candidate; not a dietary exposure.

unresolved: Kidney bismuth time course shown only in Figure 2G; values not recorded.
regulatory_or_exposure: Authors cite a documented plasma bismuth safety level of 50 µg/L and alarm level of 100 µg/L from earlier literature (p. 11).
non_numeric_findings: Bismuth compounds given alone caused no or negligible increase in blood urea nitrogen in mice (Figure 2B, p. 2).
Authors state bismuth reaches its highest visceral concentrations in kidney proximal tubule cells (p. 2, background).
